title: Derry Girls, deceit and Taskmaster campaign family
slide_intent: Compare programme variation against shared attribution, because a broadcaster must hold several distinct tones together.
strategic_value: Consistent upper-left green 4 marks can connect comedy, drama and entertainment while preserving each show’s own imagery and lettering.
demonstration: Three horizontal campaign artworks stack vertically: Derry Girls pairs a cast photograph with angled lettering, deceit pairs a portrait with textured thin letters, and Taskmaster pairs a theatrical ensemble with widely spaced lettering.
practical_value: Identify which elements can stay fixed across a campaign family while title treatments and photographs change.

content_islands.name: Derry Girls panel
content_islands.spec: Place the cast and energetic angled title in the top panel, retaining the small green 4 at upper left.

content_islands.name: deceit panel
content_islands.spec: Use the split-tone portrait and textured lowercase title in the middle panel.

content_islands.name: Taskmaster panel
content_islands.spec: Keep the theatrical scene and broad title across the lower panel, with the same small broadcaster position.

reference_purposes.Intent: Pentagram’s accompanying case study explains that show color and typography align with the masterbrand while allowing individual tonal flexibility.
reference_purposes.Expression: Three horizontal campaign artworks stack vertically: Derry Girls pairs a cast photograph with angled lettering, deceit pairs a portrait with textured thin letters, and Taskmaster pairs a theatrical ensemble with widely spaced lettering.
reference_purposes.Application: The source demonstrates this treatment in three programme campaign artworks.
